Class ReviewSystem

java.lang.Object
foodreview.ReviewSystem
public class ReviewSystem extends Object
This class consists exclusively of instance methods that are designed to display information and handle user interaction.

This is the main 'VIEW' and 'CONTROLLER' of the Model-View-Controller architectural pattern. It is meant to handle all UI and handle all user interaction with the UI. When a user interacts with the program, it directly calls the Model (DatabaseHandler to do its job in relation to the chosen task. It also passes all necessary information along, sometimes in the form of a Review object. The UI is designed to have a console on the right-hand side, displaying any output for the user to read. The rest of the UI is designed with a CardLayout in mind, treating each page like a card in a deck that can be switched to when told so.

The user is asked to give basic database information, which is then used to display review information as well as add, remove, find and update review records in the database. This means that this class relies heavily on the DatabaseHandler to do most of the actual functionality in regard to JDBC interactions, Review for object storage and passing, and a multitude of JComponent objects.

  • Method Details

    • initGui

      private void initGui()
      Initializes the core UI components and displays the first page createLoginPage().

      This method sets up the main JFrame, CardLayout and console (JTextArea. It initializes all pages (Login Page,Main Menu Page, Add Review Page, Find Review Page Average Review Page). These pages are then added to the cardlayout and the Login Page is selected to be displayed to the user.

    • mainMenuPage

      private JPanel mainMenuPage()
      Creates the main menu panel featuring a data table and navigational buttons.

      This method creates a JTable with a DefaultTableModel to display review information. To allow users to interact with the data, it constructs a grid of buttons that, when pressed, do a specific function. Some will switch the page using the navigation system. This can be seen with the buttons: Add Review, Find Review, Update Review and Average Review. For Update review, it even takes the data of the selected review from the data table to be used in the next page. Others will simply send the selected review's data and chosen function to the Model to be completed and returned.

      Returns:
      JPanel of the created main menu page, complete with all listeners and JComponents.

    • createLoginPage

      private JPanel createLoginPage()
      Create the initial page for database authentication.

      This method creates a panel which features input fields to take the server address, username and password of a MySQL server from the user. It features a single 'OK' button for the user to tell the program they are ready to send their input information.

      When the user presses the 'OK' button, an action listener instantiates the dbHandler using the information from the text field, where it attempts to connect to the database. If it's able to connect, it switches the page to the main menu page using the navigation system. If it fails, it alerts the user that something went wrong and to try again.

      Returns:
      JPanel of the created login page, complete with all listeners and JComponents.

    • addReviewPage

      private JPanel addReviewPage()
      Creates the input page for adding a new review to the system.

      This method features multiple text fields and dropdowns for the user to input and select data for a new Food Review. It features a single 'OK' button for the user to tell the program they are ready to send their input information.

      The featured fields are:
      • A text field for the food's name.
      • An optional text field for the food's subtype.
      • An optional text field for the review location.
      • A text field for the date that it was eaten.
      • A dropdown for the Category.
      • A dropdown for the rating (0-10).

      It handles optional data from the subtype and location fields by setting them to null if they are empty strings before calling the newReviewHandler(String, int, Category, String, String, String) method to create the review object and add it to the database.

      The 'OK' button takes the input data and sends it to newReviewHandler(String, int, Category, String, String, String), where the data is validated, and it returns to let the action listener know if it successfully added the review to the database. If it passes, it clears the fields. It also features a back button, which clears the fields and returns the page to the main menu.

      Returns:
      JPanel of the created add review page, complete with all listeners and JComponents.

    • findReviewPage

      private JPanel findReviewPage()
      Creates the find review page for locating specific reviews within the database.

      This method creates a panel that features input fields for a review's name and optional subtype along with an 'OK' button. The 'OK' button triggers an action listener, where if the subtype is empty, sets them to null. It then calls findReviewHandler(String, String) with the name and subtype, receiving a boolean that represents if the data was found our not. If it was found, it clears the text fields.

      Returns:
      JPanel of the created find review page, complete with all listeners and JComponents.

    • updateReviewPage

      private JPanel updateReviewPage(Review rev)
      Creates the update page for updating a pre-existing review, selected from the main menu.

      This method features multiple text fields and dropdowns for the user to input and select data to update the review. It features a single 'OK' button for the user to tell the program they are ready to send their input information.

      The featured fields are:
      • A text field for the food's name.
      • An optional text field for the food's subtype.
      • An optional text field for the review location.
      • A text field for the date that it was eaten.
      • A dropdown for the Category.
      • A dropdown for the rating (0-10).

      These fields are all pre-filled with the information of the given Review object that was passed to it. This allows the user to easily see what the old review was and what they want to edit.

      The 'OK' button takes the input data and sends it to updReviewHandler(int, String, int, Category, String, String, String), where the data is validated, and it returns to let the action listener know if it successfully updated the review. If it passes, it clears the fields. It also features a back button, which clears the fields and returns the page to the main menu. This page is deleted upon completion of the task.

      Parameters:
      rev - The Review object that was selected by the user on the Main Menu to be updated.
      Returns:
      JPanel of the created update review page, complete with all listeners and JComponents.

    • avgReviewPage

      private JPanel avgReviewPage()
      Creates a page for the user to select a category of food reviews to be calculated into an average review, filtered by category.

      This method creates a panel which features a single dropdown of categories, and an 'OK' button for the user to alert the system they are ready for the average of the selected category. It also features a back button, which resets the dropdown and returns to the main menu.

      When the 'OK' button is pressed, avgReviewHandler(Category) is called and returns a boolean. If it passes, it resets the dropdown.

      Returns:

    • refreshListHandler

      private void refreshListHandler()
      Synchronizes the UI table in mainMenuPage() with the current state of the database.

      This method clears all existing rows in the tableModel and fetches a refreshed list of Review objects from the DatabaseHandler.getAll() method. It iterates through the returned list, converting each object into row format for the table to display. For visual clarity, subtype and location are converted to 'N/A' if they are null.

    • newReviewHandler

      private boolean newReviewHandler(String name, int rating, Category cat, String subtype, String location, String date)
      Processes and validates new review data before attempting to create the object and send to the database to be saved. This method does the following:
      1. Generates a unique ID using DatabaseHandler.idGenerator().
      2. Validates the format and length of name, subtype, location, and date
      3. Standardizes string formatting using stringFormatter(String).
      4. Constructs a Review object and passes it to DatabaseHandler.addReview(Review) to be saved to the database.

      If any data validation fails or the database fails to save, it displays an error message to the user and the process is aborted.

      Parameters:
      name - The name of the food.
      rating - The int rating of the review.
      cat - The Category enum value.
      subtype - The optional subtype, can be null.
      location - The optional location, can be null.
      date - The string representing the date (YYY-MM-DD).
      Returns:
      true if the review was successfully validated and added; false if any validation failed or database insertion failed.

    • remReviewHandler

      private boolean remReviewHandler(String input)
      Removes a given review from the system based on the provided ID string.

      This method validates that the id input is a valid, positive integer. It then validates that it actually exists in the database using the DatabaseHandler.findReview(int) method. It logs the details of the review to the user and removes it from the database with DatabaseHandler.remReview(int)

      If it fails at any point in validating the id or interacting with the database, it returns false and alerts the user. Otherwise, it alerts the user it was removed successfully and returns true.

      Parameters:
      input - The ID string retrieved from the UI table.
      Returns:
      true if the review was successfully found and deleted from the database; false if the ID was invalid, not found or a database error occurred.

    • findReviewHandler

      private boolean findReviewHandler(String name, String subtype)
      Validates search criteria and queries the database for reviews matching the information.

      This method validates that the name and optional subtype meet length and character requirements. If the subtype is empty, it calls the DatabaseHandler.findReview(String) with only the name parameter. Otherwise, it calls DatabaseHandler.findReview(String, String) with both to retrieve results. Matching reviews are then displayed to the user. If no matches are found, a failure message is instead displayed.

      Parameters:
      name - The name of the food being searched.
      subtype - The optional subtype to refine the search.
      Returns:
      true if at least one matching review was found; false if no reviews were found or a database error occurred.

    • updReviewLocationHandler

      private Review updReviewLocationHandler(String input)
      locates and retrieves a review with the matching ID input for the update page.

      This method parses the ID from the provided string and verifies its existence in the database. If found, the Review object is returned. If the ID is invalid or the record doesn't exist in the database, the user is alerted and it returns null.

      Parameters:
      input - The ID string retrieved from the UI table.
      Returns:
      Review object if successfully found; null if the ID is invalid, the review doesn't exist or a database error occurs.

    • updReviewHandler

      private boolean updReviewHandler(int id, String name, int rating, Category cat, String subtype, String location, String date)
      Takes review data then validates it, creating a review from the information and passing it to update an existing record in the database. This method does the following:
      1. Validates the format and length of name, subtype, location, and date
      2. Standardizes string formatting using stringFormatter(String).
      3. Gathers the old ID and constructs a Review object, passing it to DatabaseHandler.updateReview(int, Review) to be saved to the database.

      If any data validation fails or the database fails to update, it displays an error message to the user and the process.

      Parameters:
      id - The unique ID of the review being updated.
      name - The updated name of the food item.
      rating - The updated rating of the review.
      cat - The updated category of the review.
      subtype - The updated subtype of the review.
      location - The updated location of the review.
      date - The updated date of the review.
      Returns:
      true if validation passed and the database was updated; false if validation failed or an error occurred.

    • avgReviewHandler

      private boolean avgReviewHandler(Category category)
      Retrieves and displays the average rating for a given category.

      This method calls DatabaseHandler.getAverage(Category) to perform calculations the ratings of all records matching the given Category. If an average that's 0 or more is returned, the result is formatted to two decimal places and displayed to the user. If the database returns a negative value, a failure message is displayed to the user.

      Parameters:
      category - The Category to be averaged.
      Returns:
      true if the average was successfully retried and displayed; false if the calculation failed or no data was found.

    • dispAllHandler

      private void dispAllHandler()
      Retrives all reviews from the database and prints them to the console.

      This method retries the complete list of Review objects using the DatabaseHandler.getAll() method. It iterates through the returned list, printing each review's details using the Review.consoleToString() method for visual clarity. After the process is complete, it re-enables all buttons for user interaction. If the database is empty, alerts the user.

    • stringFormatter

      private String stringFormatter(String input)
      Formats a string to title case, ensuring consistent data entry.

      This method splits the given input into words and capitalizes the first letter of each word utilizing a for each loop. Every other letter is made to be lowercase. Use this to standardize text input before storage in the database.

      Parameters:
      input - The text to be formatted.
      Returns:
      String, formatted to title-case;
